title: Adaptive-window token valuation & microbilling bridge for streaming requests
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Problem: Our current billing pipeline attributes token costs using ingestion-time windows and naive dedupe that breaks for long-lived streaming sessions and multi-part chunked responses. Late-arriving events (network retries, out-of-order shards) cause either double-billing or missing charges, and tenants with high variability (low-latency mobile clients) see noisy spikes. Goal: Build a streaming-aware microbilling bridge that performs event-time aligned token valuation with adaptive watermarking, deterministic request fingerprints for idempotent dedupe, and a tenant-configurable grace window. The bridge should operate as a lightweight pre-aggregation layer between the streaming ingestion gateway and the existing ledger reconciler so we can deploy it incrementally without changing downstream billing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Event-time watermarking applied per-tenant with default 2s but adjustable via tenant config
Deterministic request fingerprint computed from (tenant, request_id, trace_id, first_token_hash) and used for idempotent dedupe
Late-arrival correction: events arriving within grace window are merged into prior windows without creating new invoices or duplicate charges
End-to-end e2e sim shows <0.5% billing variance vs ground truth in high-lateness synthetic traces and <0.1% regressions on baseline workloads
Canary rollout plan documented and automated: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on >1% anomaly in per-tenant cost differential
Smoke and regression dashboards added to console: per-tenant token delta, late-arrival rate, dedupe hit-rate, and cost delta histogram
notes: 2025-11-03 - Kickoff: scoped MVP as pre-aggregation bridge; decided to keep existing ledger contract stable and emit reconciler-compatible events.
2025-11-05 - Design review: PM (Aria Chen) suggested tenant-level grace window config rather than global to reduce false positives on enterprise customers.
2025-11-07 - Trade-off: We debated stateful per-partition retention vs compacted tombstones for dedupe tracking. Opted for compacted RocksDB table with TTL to bound disk growth.
2025-11-10 - Prototype: fingerprint algorithm implemented in Rust worker. Using sha256 over canonicalized tuple (tenant, request_id, first_token_hash, start_ts) to preserve determinism across SDKs.

2025-11-12 - Perf: prototype processes 25k RTP (requests/sec) per core with p95 latency 8ms for in-memory paths. Disk-backed dedupe path p95 ~42ms; acceptable for business tier but we will route enterprise to reserved pool.
2025-11-14 - Security/Privacy note: fingerprints are salted with tenant-specific secret stored in KMS; salt rotation strategy documented in Confluence.

2025-11-16 - Integration: added adapters to emit reconciler-compatible 'valuation_delta' events to the existing kafka.topic.billing. Ran integration tests against staging ledger, no schema changes required.

2025-11-18 - Cost simulation: ran Monte Carlo sim across 500 tenant traces with heavy late-arrivals (50ms-15s). Adaptive watermark reduced duplicate charges by 92% vs ingestion-time windows with similar compute cost.

2025-11-20 - Blocker identified: an edge-case where trace_id is missing from some legacy SDKs. Decided fallback: prefer request_id then trace_id then synthetic ordered-offset. Added compatibility layer and created follow-up ENG-91401 to retrofit SDKs.
